note: Identifies organisational learning as the mechanism between adoption and benefit, which is a capability an audit can assess.
title: Leveraging generative artificial intelligence for sustainable business model innovation in production systems
explain_beginner: This study looks at how factories can use generative AI to make their business practices more sustainable. The researchers surveyed 402 manufacturing start-ups in China. They found that when companies adopt generative AI, it helps them learn in two ways: by improving what they already do and by discovering new things. Both types of learning then lead to more sustainable business models. The study also found that there is no single recipe for success, as different combinations of factors can work. This matters because it shows that AI's benefits depend on how well a company learns and adapts, not just on the technology itself.
explain_business: This research indicates that generative AI can drive sustainable business model innovation, but the benefit depends on organisational learning. Surveying 402 Chinese manufacturing start-ups, the study found that AI adoption improves both exploitative and exploratory learning, which then lead to sustainable innovation. The effect is moderated by international entrepreneurship orientation and AI education. There is no one-size-fits-all approach, as multiple factor combinations can yield high performance. For executives, this means investing in AI alone is not enough. Decisions should include assessing and building learning capabilities, and considering context like global orientation and training, to turn AI into tangible sustainability outcomes.
explain_practitioner: The authors propose the GAI&ABC model, integrating generative AI adoption with the Antecedents-Behaviour-Consequences framework. Using survey data from 402 Chinese manufacturing start-ups and PLS-SEM, they tested mediating roles of GAI-powered exploitative and exploratory learning, with international entrepreneurship orientation and GAI education as moderators. Results show GAI adoption significantly enhances exploitative learning (β=0.439) and exploratory learning (β=0.444), which in turn drive sustainable business model innovation (β=0.254 and 0.353, respectively). Additionally, fsQCA identified four configurations leading to high SBMI performance, underscoring implementation complexity. The key contribution is a theoretical framework linking GAI adoption, organisational learning, and contextual factors to SBMI.
